questions.stem: What is the main indication for radical cystectomy?
Name one less common indication for radical cystectomy.
questions.answer: Neurogenic bladder, chronic urinary obstruction or pelvic malignancy

questions.stem: Which organs are removed in men during radical cystectomy?
questions.answer: Bladder, prostate, seminal vesicles and urethra

questions.stem: Which structures are removed in women during radical cystectomy?
questions.answer: Bladder, urethra, anterior vaginal wall, uterus, both ovaries and fallopian tubes

questions.stem: At the end of radical cystectomy, urinary diversion is made to the colon or ____.
Anaesthesia and positioning for radical cystectomy are similar to which other operation?
What does the bowel component of radical cystectomy add to the operation?
questions.answer: Longer operating time and bacteraemia risk

questions.stem: Which three things should be assessed before radical cystectomy?
Before radical cystectomy, the team should book a ____.
Why consider preoperative IV fluids before radical cystectomy?
questions.answer: To offset losses from bowel preparation

questions.stem: How should an epidural be used during radical cystectomy, given how painful the operation is?
Which patient positioning is used for radical cystectomy?
options: Lithotomy, with or without head down

questions.stem: Which anaesthetic technique is used for radical cystectomy?
When should cell salvage be stopped during radical cystectomy?
options: At the start of the operation

questions.stem: Which three items should be ready for the intraoperative care of radical cystectomy?
questions.answer: Large-bore IV access, blood warmer, blood available in theatre
